task_instance: Scaffold a foundry-agents.json manifest with one agent (alert-triage) and a sync script, then attempt to actually create/sync that agent into a live Azure AI Foundry project via the Agent Service REST API (POST {projectEndpoint}/agents/{agentName}?api-version=2025-11-15-preview), as the skill's core deliverable requires.
blocker_detail: The skill's actual purpose is server-side: registering/updating a prompt agent inside a real Azure AI Foundry project so it is immediately invocable there. That requires (1) an existing Azure subscription with an AI Foundry project and a deployed model, (2) the Azure CLI authenticated (az login) as a principal holding the 'Azure AI User' role on that project, and (3) a bearer token from `az account get-access-token --resource https://ai.azure.com/` to call the REST API. None of these exist in this sandbox: the `az` CLI is not installed, there are no AZURE_* credentials/env vars, and obtaining/using such account-bound Azure credentials to sign into a real cloud subscription is exactly the kind of credential/account-bound action the safety rules prohibit. I could produce the manifest and sync script (the scaffolding half of the skill), but running the sync script confirmed it fails immediately at `az account set` because there is no Azure CLI or authenticated account available -- there is no live Foundry project to register an agent into in this runtime.
evidence: Created /tmp/.../infra/foundry-agents.json with one agent definition (useCaseId=alert-triage) and /tmp/.../infra/scripts/sync-foundry-agents.sh (bash translation of the skill's PowerShell sync template, using az + curl). Checked `which az` -> not found; `env | grep -i AZURE` -> no Azure credentials present. Ran the sync script against a placeholder subscription/endpoint: output was `sync-foundry-agents.sh: line 14: az: command not found`, confirming the core deliverable (an actual POST to a live Foundry project's Agent Service that creates/updates an agent) cannot be executed in this runtime without an Azure account, a Foundry project, and az CLI authentication, which are both unavailable and off-limits under the safety rules (no credentials/account-bound services).
